radiusSource: Radius 3.77 Jupiter radii and temperature 2700 K: the BT-Settl fit with extinction to the combined VLT/MUSE and SINFONI spectra of Stolker et al. (2021, AJ; doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ac2c7f; arXiv:2110.04307), Table 4: 269,524.8 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. A model radius, not a measured diameter. Cugno et al. (2024, arXiv:2404.07086) refit the same spectra with JWST/MIRI and find 3.60 to 3.71 and 2700 to 2719 K. GM from the evolutionary-model mass 33 +/- 10 Jupiter masses of Xuan et al. (2024, arXiv:2405.13128, Table 1) times Jupiter's GM; published masses range from about 10 to 40. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.
orbitalPeriodSource: Derived: Kepler's third law with the sample's semi-major axis 101.428 au and total mass 1.0772 solar masses, 984.2 years of 365.25 d. Venkatesan et al. (2025, ApJ 993, 69; arXiv:2509.20621), the adopted GRAVLowRV fit: orbitize! parallel-tempered MCMC on eight literature positions (Table 2), four VLTI/GRAVITY positions (Table 3) and the CRIRES differential radial velocity 2.0 +/- 0.4 km/s (Table 4), total mass 1.05 +/- 0.07 solar masses and parallax 6.489 +/- 0.029 mas, tau from MJD 58849. They release no posterior; their Table 6 medians are a 97.71 au, e 0.35, i 48.18, omega 175.82, Omega 257.08 degrees, tau 0.32. This run used 20 temperatures and 100 walkers for 15,000 burn-in and 10,000 saved steps against their 1000 walkers and 300,000 steps. The maximum of orbitize!'s own posterior (ln L -43.16), refined with Nelder-Mead from the twenty best of 100,000 samples, from orbitize! 3.4.0 run on that paper's published measurements and priors (tools/objects/hosted-orbits/orbitize-fit.py, src/objects/gq-lup-b/source/orbits/fit.json).

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray. No image, colour, map or oblateness of GQ Lup b is measured; only its size, mass and orbit are.
